newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Teva denies owing huge sum in VAT.
newsitem.headline: Teva denies owing huge sum in VAT.

text.p: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd on Monday denied a news report that the Israeli government was demanding it pay an "enormous amount" in back payments of value added tax (VAT).
The company's chief financial officer Dan Suesskind told Reuters that the amount in question was $4 million. "This for a company like Teva is not a huge amount," he said.

The report, which appeared on a local financial news wire, caused the Tel Aviv share to decline 1.5 percent to 208.07 shekels in the afternoon, after it had risen earlier on a strong second-quarter earnings report, traders said.
Suesskind said the company believes the government's claim is without merit.
He said the pharmaceutical industry offers discounts to Israeli health funds on purchases made by the funds' clients at private pharmacies.

"Two years ago we went to the VAT authorities and asked them how to relate to the discounts for VAT purposes. We got from them a precise ruling...which said we can deduct it from our invoices," Suesskind said.
"After two years they have challenged their own ruling and are claiming money."
Suesskind said company and government officials were to meet soon to discuss the matter.
A spokeswoman for the customs and VAT authority said she could not comment on the matter.
